before: Text boxes in headers and footers render and replicate edits made through automation, but the editor refuses to enter them, and legacy VML text boxes refuse every move, resize and delete.
after: The editor enters a header or footer text box and writes its edits as ordinary operations on that part. An upright legacy VML text box moves, resizes and deletes through the existing drawing operations, which rewrite only the geometry entries of its style attribute.
reason: Edits use the existing paragraph, run and drawing operations on an existing part. Shared nodes, text offsets, operation shapes and package serialization remain unchanged; a legacy geometry edit replicates as the changed shape node.
